og.og:description: The Northern Illinois Transit Authority (NITA) is proud to provide reduced fares to low income transit riders. The program, which started in 2024,…
og.og:image:alt: The Northern Illinois Transit Authority (NITA) is proud to provide reduced fares to low income transit riders. The program, which started in 2024, expanded regionwide in 2026 and allows residents of the NITA region who qualify for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) or Illinois Department of Human Services' FRESH Program to take CTA, Metra, or Pace at a reduced price. Applications are available at  GetAccess.org .   The Access Program is an expansion of NITA's  Ride Free and Reduced Fare  programs, which will continue to be available to older adults and individuals with disabilities.

og.og:image:alt: NITA launched the Access to Transit program in 2014 (under its predecessor the RTA) as a means to improve access to the regional transit system for pedestrians and bicyclists, thereby implementing recommendations from planning studies completed through NITA's  Community Planning  program. To date, the program has funded 71 projects in municipalities throughout the region for a total investment of $34.4 million. Detailed information on past projects is available on NITA's Data Portal.  Read the latest success stories in the 2025 Local Planning Annual Report .

description: Under NITA, Access — a popular fare pilot that enables Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) recipients to ride Metra at a reduced fare —…

og.og:title: Northern Illinois Transit Authority | NITA expands income-based reduced fare pilot Access across Metra, CTA, and Pace
og.og:description: Under NITA, Access — a popular fare pilot that enables Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) recipients to ride Metra at a reduced fare —…
og.og:image:alt: Under NITA, Access — a popular fare pilot that enables Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) recipients to ride Metra at a reduced fare — expanded to CTA and Pace on October 1. The NITA Board of Directors met for the first time on September 10 and hit the ground running by approving this Access Pilot Program expansion. With the Board’s action to expand the program, those who qualify can now ride CTA and Pace at 50 percent off, making CTA bus rides $1.10 and L rides $1.25, and Pace bus rides only $1. “By making Access available across CTA, Metra and Pace, we’re turning a successful pilot into a regional benefit and making transit more equitable and affordable for riders who need it most.” Current Access riders There are currently 9,000 active Access permits being used on Metra. One Metra rider enrolled in the Access Pilot Program, Tiana Love of Chicago, said she and her family ride Metra much more often now that she’s able to purchase tickets at a reduced fare.

headings: NITA expands income-based reduced fare pilot Access across Metra, CTA, and Pace October 1, 2026
